_comment: Clarity in the Quran (@ClarityInTheQuran, UC0eBu0ZXcF20pTAG3lUnPXA) localized metadata, 2026-08-22. YouTube serves a video's localized title and description to viewers whose app language matches, so ONE write per video reaches a new language audience on the ENTIRE back catalogue, retroactively. This is a first-class Data API feature (videos.update, part=snippet,localizations) — nothing here bends a rule.
_why_this_exists: vidIQ keyword research, 2026-08-22. 'quran explained in english' = 5,268 searches/month. Bare 'quran' = 1,398,036/month, of which the US is 6.5%. 'surah' = 283,511/month, of which Bangladesh alone is 47.7% and Pakistan 28.4%. 'islamic video' = 662,172/month, 90% Bangladesh + Pakistan combined. The reference channel this one is modelled on, @deepmadesimple, is US-English Bible study — its audience and its language are the same thing. Clarity copied the format into a niche where they are not. English is not the language of this channel's market; it is the language of its template.
_default_language: YouTube ignores localizations unless the video's snippet.defaultLanguage is set. It is unset on every upload here, so the script sets it to 'en' in the SAME write that adds the localizations. Miss this and the write succeeds and does nothing — the worst kind of failure.
_single_write: Title, defaultLanguage and localizations land in one fetch-mutate-write per video, for the reason set_packaging already documents: videos.list is read-after-write eventually consistent, so a second write can read back a pre-write snippet and undo the first.
_translation_provenance: Written, not machine-piped. Surah names use their standard Arabic forms; the Urdu keeps Quranic terms in their Arabic spelling as Urdu religious register actually does rather than transliterating them phonetically. THIS CHANNEL ALREADY CARRIES A PUBLIC 'AI BE AWARE' COMMENT — a clumsy translation in a language the owner does not read would be that same wound, reopened, in a market that matters more. Six videos first, deliberately: they carry ~80% of lifetime views, and they are a small enough tranche for a native speaker to check before the remaining twelve follow.
_scope: Six videos = 2,059 of 2,561 lifetime views. Arabic and Urdu only. Bengali is the single largest opportunity in the data (47.7% of 'surah') and is deliberately NOT here: it is the language I can least vouch for unreviewed, and it deserves a native pass rather than a confident guess.
